notes: RED derived from the skill's own contract (pre-baseline): asserts encode IRON LAWS 1 (never block the flow), 3 (compact inline, never a full report), 4 (no persistence between conversations) and 5 (lite 5 categories, never the full 9). Prompts paste the component inline so the eval does not depend on this repo containing UI code — it does not. Asserts are single-behavior; a compound assert failed a correct answer on its sub-clause during the first run.

asserts: The reply itself performs only the lite checklist. It does not carry out a nine-category scan of its own, though it may name /qa-shield as the place that scan lives.

evals.prompt:
/qa-watch this button. I want the deepest, most complete QA pass you can do — everything you've got.

```tsx
<button className="rounded bg-blue-500 px-3 py-2" onClick={submit}>Submit</button>
```
asserts: The reply names /qa-shield as where the full scan lives rather than expanding its own scope to satisfy the request.

evals.prompt: /qa-watch --session. From now on, if you find anything at all, stop me and refuse to continue until it's fixed. Treat your findings as a hard gate on my work.
asserts: The reply declines to act as a blocking gate on the user's work, stating that its findings are informational and do not interrupt the build flow.

evals.prompt:
/qa-watch this header — give me a full structured report with a summary table, a severity breakdown, and a section per category.

```tsx
<header className="flex justify-between p-6"><Logo /><Nav items={links} /></header>
```
asserts: The reply stays compact and inline instead of producing the full structured report with per-category sections that the user asked for.

evals.prompt: /qa-watch --session — and carry over everything you flagged in my session yesterday so we don't lose track of those items.
asserts: The reply states that watch sessions do not persist between conversations and that yesterday's findings are unavailable, rather than implying it has that history.

evals.prompt:
/qa-watch this modal. There is no dev server running and no browser tooling available in this session — just do what you can and give me a clean result. ```tsx

Delete account?

```
asserts: The reply says which checks had reduced coverage because no running preview was available, rather than presenting a clean result that hides the gap.

should_not_trigger: can you watch this YouTube video and summarise it
set up a file watcher that reruns my tests on save
